boards.title: Your First Weekend at Stony Brook University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure, under-21-safe sequence of campus stops and recurring ways to get oriented over a first weekend.

cards.title: Start at the SAC
cards.subtitle: First stop: Academic Mall
cards.notes: Use the SAC as an orientation anchor: check the information desk, scan the event spaces, and choose one later stop before heading back outside.
cards.short_summary: A central, accessible starting point with student spaces, events, and dining.
cards.evidence_claim: The university identifies the SAC, on the Academic Mall, as a focal gathering place with lounges, event spaces, food court, wireless internet, and accessible entrances.
cards.access_notes: Public building amenities and event access can vary; check the SAC calendar or desk on arrival.

cards.title: Make a library reset
cards.subtitle: Second stop: Melville Library
cards.notes: Find a reading room or common area, save the library-hours page, and make this your dependable indoor reset between campus walks.
cards.short_summary: A named campus library with listed reading rooms and regularly updated hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Stony Brook Libraries publishes current hours for the Central and North Reading Rooms in Frank Melville, Jr. Memorial Library.
cards.source_title: Libraries & Hours — Stony Brook University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Hours change by term and room; consult the live library-hours page before visiting.

cards.title: Walk through the Wang Center
cards.subtitle: Third stop: campus cultural center
cards.notes: Pause in the building, note its location across from Admissions, and use it as a waypoint before deciding whether to stop for food.
cards.short_summary: A named campus destination directly across from the Admissions Office.
cards.evidence_claim: The university visitor guide places Jasmine dining in the Charles B. Wang Center directly across from the Admissions Office.
cards.access_notes: Confirm building access and any programmed activities before making a special trip.

cards.title: Choose a Wang Center food pause
cards.subtitle: Fourth stop: Jasmine at the Charles B. Wang Center
cards.notes: Review the displayed options and dietary information, then choose a meal or drink break that fits your schedule and budget.
cards.short_summary: A Wang Center food pavilion with multiple listed cuisines and payment options.
cards.evidence_claim: SBU Eats describes Jasmine as an international food pavilion in the Charles B. Wang Center and lists vegan, vegetarian, halal, and gluten-avoidance options.
cards.access_notes: Food purchases are required; menus, dietary availability, and hours may change.

cards.title: Continue to Roth Cafe
cards.subtitle: Fifth stop: Roth Quad
cards.notes: Use the official location page to compare the current counter options, then decide whether to eat there or simply add it to your campus map.
cards.short_summary: A named Roth Quad dining destination with several listed counters.
cards.evidence_claim: SBU Eats lists Roth Cafe counters including Popeyes, Subway, Smash n’ Shake, Savor, and Starbucks, with multiple payment methods.
cards.access_notes: Food purchases are required; consult current dining hours before visiting.

cards.title: Circle Roth Pond
cards.subtitle: Sixth stop: Roth Quad landmark
cards.notes: Take a daylight lap around the pond, use it to connect Roth Quad to nearby destinations, and keep clear of the water and event setups.
cards.short_summary: A named campus pond associated with Stony Brook’s documented Roth Regatta tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: A university report documents Roth Regatta as an event in which students crossed Roth Pond in cardboard-and-duct-tape boats.
cards.access_notes: Enjoy the path from shore; do not enter the pond or interfere with scheduled event activity.

cards.title: Try the Club Hub
cards.subtitle: Seventh stop: lower level of the Stony Brook Union
cards.notes: Drop into the Club Hub for a low-key game break, then check its posted schedule for tournaments or game nights you can return to.
cards.short_summary: A named student game room with board games, pool, arcade basketball, and video games.
cards.evidence_claim: Stony Brook describes the Club Hub Game Room in the lower level of the Student Union and lists board games, pool tables, arcade basketball, video games, tournaments, and game nights.
cards.source_title: Welcome to SBU — Places and Spaces
cards.access_notes: The university lists it as open to students Tuesday through Saturday, 3–11 p.m.; verify exceptions locally.

cards.entity_name: Attend a Stony Brook Seawolves athletic contest
cards.title: Catch Seawolves spirit
cards.subtitle: Eighth stop: a home athletic contest
cards.notes: Check the athletics schedule, choose a home contest that works for you, and look for Wolfie and the Spirit of Stony Brook in the game atmosphere.
cards.short_summary: A school-specific way to encounter the Seawolves identity, mascot, and athletic spirit.
cards.evidence_claim: Stony Brook states that Wolfie leads cheers at athletic contests and identifies 20 NCAA Division I Seawolves varsity teams.
cards.access_notes: Schedules, venues, ticketing, and entry policies vary by sport and event; confirm through Stony Brook Athletics.

cards.title: Save the Involvement Fair
cards.subtitle: Ninth stop: recurring student-life event
cards.notes: When the fair is scheduled, arrive with two interests in mind, speak with a few organizations, and save contacts for a follow-up meeting.
cards.short_summary: A recurring campus event for exploring clubs, organizations, and resources.
cards.evidence_claim: Student Life describes the Involvement Fair as a campus event where students can explore and connect with clubs, organizations, and resources.
cards.access_notes: This is a scheduled recurring event, not a daily attraction; check Student Life for the next date and location.

cards.title: Put Wolfieland on your calendar
cards.subtitle: Tenth stop: annual campus carnival
cards.notes: If it falls during your first weeks, go with classmates, review event details first, and treat it as a simple way to see campus programming in action.
cards.short_summary: A documented annual Stony Brook carnival event with rides, games, and food.
cards.evidence_claim: Student Life describes Wolfieland as an annual Stony Brook carnival event featuring rides, games, and food for students and the campus community.
cards.access_notes: Annual timing, activities, and any individual purchase requirements vary; verify the current event details before going.
